title: Rakul Preet Singh Denies Link to IT Searches, Demands Retractions
excerpt: The actress called reports linking her to the Income Tax Department's Mumbai searches "false, malicious and speculative," saying she has paid taxes since age 20 and urging retractions.
body:
• Actress Rakul Preet Singh has denied that the Income Tax Department's recent search operations have anything to do with her, calling reports linking her to the action "false, malicious and speculative."
  • In a strongly worded public statement, she said she has been paying taxes since age 20, denied involvement in illegal foreign remittances or holding benami property, and urged outlets that carried the claims to retract them.
  • The searches were carried out roughly a week ago across multiple locations in Mumbai, with reports linking them to filmmaker Vashu Bhagnani and entities associated with Pooja Entertainment over suspected financial irregularities.
  • No official findings from the searches have been made public so far; the department has not announced any conclusion regarding tax evasion or money laundering.

The statement

Actress Rakul Preet Singh on Monday broke her silence on media reports linking her name to recent Income Tax Department searches in Mumbai, issuing a detailed public note to deny any connection with the action. "Let's therefore set the record straight once for all. The search was not pertaining to me," she wrote.

In the statement, the actress — known for her work across Hindi, Telugu and Tamil cinema — pushed back hard at what she described as sensationalized coverage. "It's heartbreaking to see that there's a growing trend amongst the self styled online reporters & some main stream media journalists to sensationalise the news without verifying facts," she said.

She leaned on her background to make her case: a family rooted in the Armed Forces, an industry career built without a godfather, and what she describes as a long record as a law-abiding taxpayer. "I have come up through sheer hardwork & as a responsible law abiding citizen have been paying my due taxes since the age of 20 years," the statement said.

Denying the specifics

Rakul addressed the substance of the reports directly. She denied any involvement in illegal foreign remittances in a personal capacity or on behalf of any production house, and categorically denied holding benami property for anyone in India or abroad. She also said that nobody had ever gifted her any property and that she does not accept expensive gifts as a matter of principle.

"I urge all those who published these false, malicious and speculative reports to retract them and clarify the facts. I understand that everyone running a media business however big has their own commercial pressures. But it cannot come at the cost of facts. And certainly not at the cost of someone's reputation and livelihood."— Rakul Preet Singh, in her public statement

What the searches were about

Reports over the past week have said the Income Tax Department searched multiple locations in Mumbai in connection with an ongoing probe into suspected financial irregularities in the film industry. According to those reports, investigators have been examining documents and transaction records linked to filmmaker Vashu Bhagnani and entities associated with Pooja Entertainment, reportedly looking into allegations that funds may have been sent abroad in the name of film shoots, production or distribution.

The personal link in the coverage is familial: Rakul is married to actor-producer Jackky Bhagnani, the son of Vashu Bhagnani. It is that connection that appears to have pulled her name into the reporting — a linkage she now forcefully rejects.

Crucially, no official findings from the searches have been made public, and the department has not announced any conclusion regarding tax evasion or money laundering. The allegations, in other words, remain unproven as well as denied.

A familiar pattern

This is not the first time the actress's name has surfaced alongside tax-enforcement headlines. Back in 2016, she publicly denied reports that her home had been raided by Income Tax officials in the wake of the Gali Janardhana Reddy wedding, telling Deccan Chronicle at the time that "nobody checks the facts or bothers to even ask me." A decade later, her complaint — sensationalism without verification — is strikingly similar.

Why it matters for the diaspora

For the diaspora, the episode is a reminder of how quickly an unverified report can travel across borders — Gulf News readers and Indian audiences abroad saw the claims before any official word existed. Until findings are made public, the only fact on record is the denial, and reputations are the casualty in between.

What happens next

Whether the outlets Rakul named will issue the retractions she demanded remains to be seen. The larger probe into the entities linked to Pooja Entertainment continues, and the Income Tax Department has yet to release any official statement on what the searches turned up.
